From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Commitment slab & warmstart schedule — HelixThera dedicated capacity

Hi Maria / Procurement,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — attaching a concise set of dedicated reservation options tailored to HelixThera's expected inference mix. The goal here is to give you clear tradeoffs (unit cost vs. activation speed) so you can pick a commitment slab that matches your launch cadence.

Attached: helix_2026_dedicated_proposal.pdf and helix_warmstart_worksheet.xlsx (summary + sizing).

Summary (top-line):
- Option Slate (Conservative): 24 GPUs reserved (min 16 GPUs active), 12-week staged ramp. Lowest near-term Opex but longer lead to full throughput.
- Option Ramp (Balanced): 40 GPUs reserved (min 30 GPUs active), 8-week ramp with warmstart pre-warm in week 1. Best mix of latency SLOs and predictable unit costs.
- Option Anchor (Aggressive): 80 GPUs reserved (min 60 GPUs active), 4-week activation with a 2-week warm pre-warm window. Best for immediate latency/throughput at higher commit.

Notes/assumptions:
- Pricing shown is net of a standard onboarding credit; we can convert to a fixed-term discount if you prefer.
- Warmstart: we recommend a 48–72 hour progressive KV-cache warmup, plus a 7–14 day elevated pre-warm for high-traffic launch.
- Autoscaling policy: we can gate burst capacity to avoid runaway spend while maintaining headroom for spikes.
- Compliance/KMS: private key integrations supported; will confirm KMS region parity in follow-up.

Ask: please indicate a preferred option and any hard constraints on activation window or data residency. If procurement wants a single-sheet MAIP (mutual action plan) we can produce a week-by-week activation plan tied to milestones.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short sync if helpful.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Lead Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0132
Attachments: helix_2026_dedicated_proposal.pdf (proposal), helix_warmstart_worksheet.xlsx (activation worksheet)

Olga,

Appreciate the clear options — helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

2) KMS/data residency — we need keys in us-west-2 and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Is that supported out of the box or will that require an addendum?
3) Procurement asks whether a starter credit can be applied (we typically get a 10% onboarding credit on new infra contracts).

If you can confirm those three items, I'll loop in our procurement lead and legal to start a draft SOW.

Thanks,
Maria Gomez

Olga / Marissa — quick technical readout and recommendation.

Short answers to HelixThera's asks: 
- 6-week Balanced ramp: doable. Recommended reserved sizing = 40 GPUs with a minimum active floor of 28 GPUs (we can apply a 30% headroom fade in during weeks 2–3). Ramp plan:
  * Week 0: provisioning + 48–72 hr progressive KV warm (pre-warm reserved 10% of capacity)
  * Week 1–2: pilot traffic -> 40% of peak (pre-warm elevated for end-to-end flows)
  * Week 3–4: 65–80% of peak with autoscaling buffers enabled
  * Week 5–6: steady-state at target throughput (tailored batching/quantization profiles applied)

- Burst tariff: we can allow limited burst at a premium (recommended cap 20% of total additional vGPU hours per week) for weeks 2–4. Commercial team to confirm price points.

- KMS / SIEM: we support customer KMS in us-west-2 (bring-your-own-key pattern) and have a log-forwarding connector for common SIEMs. Two notes: (1) For strict U.S.-only data residency, move to Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC peering; we'll document the KMS region binding in the SOW. (2) Audit log forwarding requires a short ops-runbook and an onboarding SLA for log retention.

Attachments: sizing_calcs_helix.csv (GPU utilization model + burn forecast).

Recommendation: present the 6-week Balanced ramp as the recommended path; offer a one-time onboarding package: either a 10% credit OR 200 hours of warmstart covered by Redwood (internal commercial to choose). If procurement pushes for the credit, recommend we accept the 10% only if they commit to a 12-month reserved term.

If you want, I can produce a week-by-week MAIP and a short ops-runbook to include in the SOW.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
